title: tableSizeFor rewritten with numberOfLeadingZeros, proved equal on all 2^32 inputs
summary: The symbol table rounds a requested capacity up to a power of two with the five-shift bit smear of JDK 8's `HashMap.tableSizeFor`. A developer replaces the smear with the one-line form JDK 11 adopted, `-1 >>> Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(cap - 1)`. The regression proof compiles both versions into one program and proves them equal on every `int`, with the JDK's own bytecode of `numberOfLeadingZeros` in the proof.

change.description: Replace `n |= n >>> 1; n |= n >>> 2; ... n |= n >>> 16` with `-1 >>> Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(cap - 1)`: one intrinsic instead of five shifts and five ors, the same clamp to 1 and to the maximum capacity afterwards. It is the rewrite `java.util.HashMap` made in JDK 11. The tests for powers of two, rounding up and the ceiling all pass.

risk: None if the two forms agree everywhere, and the edges are where they might not: `cap` of 0 and 1 (where `cap - 1` is 0 or negative and `numberOfLeadingZeros` returns 32 or 0), `Integer.MIN_VALUE`, and the values just over the maximum capacity. A table that comes out one bit too small overflows its mask and corrupts lookups; one that comes out as 0 or negative fails at allocation. A reviewer can check four edges by hand and does; the proof checks the other four billion.
explanation: The regression proof puts both versions of `tableSizeFor` in one program and asks JBMC whether any `int` makes them differ. `Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros` is not a model: the tool puts the JDK's own `java.lang.Integer` class, read from the running JDK's image, on the solver's class path, so the proof is over the bytecode of the method as the JDK ships it (and so was the one in example 036 for `Math`). The solver finds no differing input in a fraction of a second, which is the proof: for all 2^32 capacities, the smear and the intrinsic produce the same power of two, with the same clamps. The property committed for the method (a power of two, at least the request, the smallest such, within the maximum) is proved of the new form as well.
resolution: Merge. The proof is the review: the JDK's rewrite was correct in the JDK and it is correct here, and the next change to this method gets the same check against this version.
provenance: Constructed from the change to `HashMap.tableSizeFor` between JDK 8 and JDK 11.

references.title: Hacker's Delight, rounding up to a power of 2 (the bit smear)
